newsitem.title: USA: Ameritech access lines up 3.3 percent in Q2.
newsitem.headline: Ameritech access lines up 3.3 percent in Q2.

text.p: Ameritech Corp said Tuesday its access lines increased by 3.3 percent in the second quarter versus last year to 20 million, while network minutes of use rose 8.6 percent.
The Baby Bell said its cellular customers grew 31 percent to 2.9 million, paging customers were up 38 percent to 1.3 million, and security monitoring customers rose 42 percent to 566,000.
Sales of call management services, including caller ID, call waiting and voice mail, posted annual growth of 22 percent, the company said.
Ameritech said it added 148,000 cellular customers during the quarter and 344,000 over the first six month -- the largest second quarter and first half gains in the company's history.
Ameritech also said it added 122,000 security monitoring customers during the quarter.

Ameritech said it continued its push to enter the long-distance market in its five-state region. Ameritech has applied for approval to provide service in Michigan, and said the Federal Communications Commission is expected to rule on that application by August 19.
"Ameritech plans to file for long distance entry in additional states in the near future," the company said in a statement.

The company said it has added 13 new cable television franchises this year, bringing to 42 the total number of its franchises covering two million people. The Ameritech cable service is available in 26 communities.

On Tuesday, Ameritech reported a 10.1 percent jump in operating earnings to $624 million from $567 million last year, and a 10.8 percent increase in operating earnings per share to $1.13 a share from $1.02. Operating results exclude a one-time charge of $87 million or $0.16 a share from a workforce restructuring at the Belgian telecommunications company Belgacom, one of its overseas investments.
Revenues rose to $3.99 billion from $3.74 billion.
Shares of Ameritech were off 10/16 at 67-11/16 in composite trading.
